source_observations.observation: session.create allocates the live session identity used by later session operations; an empty create is not durable until the first prompt persistence boundary.
source_observations.contract_relevance: A new root or branch must use one complete identity and must not be copied into a second implicit session.

source_observations.observation: session.resume reopens an addressable stored session and returns an error when the stored identity is missing.
source_observations.contract_relevance: Resume reuses the exact session and root identities; a missing identity cannot become a new session fallback.

source_observations.observation: reopen_session clears ended markers for the supplied session id before its durable history is read.
source_observations.contract_relevance: A closed parent remains an addressable lineage anchor; reopening it must not change its root or parent identity.

source_observations.anchor: def create_session(self, session_id: str, source: str, **kwargs)
source_observations.observation: SessionDB creation is keyed by the stored session id and is idempotent for a repeated create of the same row.
source_observations.contract_relevance: Repeated lineage creation with the same idempotency key reuses one identity and records no second child.

source_observations.observation: Transport loss detaches sessions for bounded recovery rather than proving that the server session was deleted.
source_observations.contract_relevance: Closed and interrupted lineage state must be reconciled or explicitly resumed, not silently replaced.

source_observations.observation: Dispatch and parse failures are explicit errors rather than successful method results.
source_observations.contract_relevance: Unknown or incompatible lineage evidence fails closed and cannot trigger an automatic new session.

states.meaning: No lineage operation is active and no session identity is selected.
A root or branch identity request is pending.
A selected session has a validated root and parent lineage.
The exact selected session identity is being resumed.
The durable session is closed or detached but remains addressable.
Creation or resume stopped before its result was safely known.
A creation result is unknown and source state must be reread first.
A known lineage or restore operation failed without a fallback.
Lineage evidence is malformed, foreign, unsupported, or unsafe.

cases.notes: An empty state has no selected identity and no lineage side effect.
An explicit root create allocates one complete root identity but remains non-durable until persistence.
A repeated root create acknowledgement reuses the same complete identity.
The first persistence boundary makes the root addressable without changing its identity.
A fork from an open durable parent preserves the root and binds the exact parent.
A closed durable parent remains an addressable fork anchor; closing is not deletion.
A repeated branch create does not create a second child or alter the parent link.
Resume returns the same branch identity, root identity, parent identity, and lineage kind.
Resuming a closed root reopens that root; it does not create a replacement.
Concurrent resume requests share one restore attempt for one exact identity.
A missing stored identity fails without silently creating a new session.
A deleted identity is not treated as a closed resumable identity.
A branch without a parent reference is incompatible.
A parent reference that is not a complete opaque ID is incompatible.
A session cannot name itself as its parent.
A parent graph that already contains the child is cyclic and stops.
A branch request for a different parent identity cannot borrow the selected root.
A deleted parent cannot be used for a new branch.
An interrupted fork keeps the existing parent selected and permits only an idempotent retry.
The same creation key may be retried after interruption without changing lineage.
An unknown branch result is delivery uncertainty, not a failure or a new-session signal.
Re-reading the server finds the original branch and prevents a duplicate creation.
A missing result after an unknown create remains failed until an explicit user choice.
Retrying an unknown create before reconciliation is incompatible and cannot duplicate a child.
An interrupted resume preserves the exact stored lineage and requires a safe reread.
Missing or mismatched compatibility evidence blocks root creation without a fallback.
A compatibility failure blocks lineage expansion even when a parent identity exists.
Unknown lineage evidence never becomes an implicit create or resume action.
Malformed lineage evidence closes the operation with one semantic failure.
A full but foreign session ID is rejected rather than mapped by prefix or similarity.
A new root is allowed only after an explicit user choice, never as automatic resume recovery.
An explicit new root has a null parent and does not inherit a previous lineage.

redaction.diagnostic_policy: stable semantic errors only; retain no raw values, paths, or payloads
